step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Using X-ray films or images): This strong, fiberlike tissue anchors theroot to the bone and cushions the surrounding bone against the shock of chewing and biting (p. 14).
Step 2 (Using X-ray films or images): When extracting a tooth, thedentist cuts the periodontal ligament that connects the tooth to the bone (p. 14).
Step 3 (Using X-ray films or images): The bony part of the upper and lower jaws that surrounds and supports the roots of the teeth and the gumsis called the alveolar bone (p. 14).
Step 4 (Using X-ray films or images): Alveolar means "hollow." The alveolar bone has hollow places, or sockets, that house the roots of the teeth (p. 14).

pamphlet_excerpts: Careers & Professional Pathways: They work directly with dentists and orthodontists and have little patient contact (p. 56).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 2: Education and Cost of Training The basic training for dentists is four years of dental schoolafter graduation from college (p. 56).

Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 3: Upon successful completion ofdental school requirements, the graduate is awarded a doctor ofdental surgery (D. D. S.) or a doctor of dental medicine (p. 56).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 4: To practice, he or she must pass both a written nationalboard and a state or regional examination (p. 56).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Careers & Professional Pathways): After passing theboards, the dental school graduate may apply to the state board of dentistry for a license to practice general dentistry (p. 56).
Step 2 (Careers & Professional Pathways): The sponsoring institution may decide whether the dentistmust pay for his or her advanced training, or whether he or sheshould receive a stipend (p. 56).
Step 3 (Careers & Professional Pathways): It is common practice tooffer paid residency programs in hospitals in the areas ofpediatric dentistry, oral surgery, and general dentistry (p. 56).
Step 4 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Postgraduate training in dental schools for the other specialtiesusually require tuition (p. 56).
